name: C0015 | R12 | PowerShell-Driven Discovery via Nested CMD
description: Detects the discovery sequence powershell -> cmd.exe -> discovery tool (net/tasklist/nltest/whoami/systeminfo/arp/wmic/ipconfig), anchored by process.entity_id - the beacon discovery batch (S4).
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S4 operator discovery (T1057/T1018/T1016/T1069/T1482) when the session beacon runs the runbook batch. Building block: ON - correlate with R10/R11 for the full chain.

## Data and schedule

Sysmon Operational, index logs-windows.sysmon_operational-c0015*. Interval 1m, look-back 5m. Sequence of 2 events (powershell -> cmd -> discovery), maxspan 30s, joined by process.entity_id / parent.entity_id within the same host.id.

## Investigation

1. Reconstruct the process chain powershell -> cmd -> tool and compare it with the C2-SIM task results for the session.
2. Distinguish a beacon discovery batch (several commands within seconds) from occasional legitimate administration.
false_positives: Administrator manually running whoami/net in a console; legitimate scripts performing discovery.
query:
sequence by host.id with maxspan=30s
  [process where event.code == "1"
     and event.type == "start"
     and process.name : "cmd.exe"
     and process.parent.name : ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
     and process.entity_id != null and not process.entity_id : ("", "{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}", "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")
  ] by process.entity_id
  [process where event.code == "1"
     and event.type == "start"
     and process.parent.name : "cmd.exe"
     and process.name : ("net.exe", "net1.exe", "tasklist.exe", "nltest.exe", "whoami.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "arp.exe", "wmic.exe", "ipconfig.exe")
     and process.parent.entity_id != null and not process.parent.entity_id : ("", "{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}", "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")
  ] by process.parent.entity_id

name: C0015 | R13 | Share Enumeration via net view or Get-SmbShare
description: Detects network share enumeration through E1 command-line classes: net.exe/net1.exe with view/use parameters, or PowerShell calling Get-SmbShare (S5, T1135).
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S5 share enumeration; a net use against a share is a precursor to lateral movement (S7).

## Data and schedule

Sysmon Operational, index logs-windows.sysmon_operational-c0015*. Interval 1m, look-back 5m.

## Investigation

Inspect the surrounding command batch to determine context; correlate net use entries with subsequent logons (R14a).
query:
any where event.code == "1"
  and event.type == "start"
  and (
    (process.name : ("net.exe", "net1.exe")
       and process.command_line : ("* view *", "* view", "* use *"))
    or
    (process.name : ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
       and process.command_line : "*Get-SmbShare*")
  )
  and process.entity_id != null and not process.entity_id : ("", "{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}", "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")

name: C0015 | R14a | Network Logon by Non-System Account
description: Detects network logon (Security 4624 LogonType 3) by a real account; the authentication layer for lateral movement hops (WMI/SMB with explicit credentials, S7/S8b).
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S7 authentication signal. Requires the Logon/Logoff audit policy (enabled by default for success).

## Data and schedule

Security channel, index logs-system.security-c0015*. Interval 1m, look-back 5m. winlog.logon.id is not populated for 4624 (SubjectLogonId=0x0) - correlate 4624 with 4672 via TargetLogonId/SubjectLogonId manually, within the same host only.

## Investigation

Match source (SubjectUserName/WorkstationName) and target; a Type-3 logon with an administrative account preceding WMI/SMB activity indicates lateral movement.
false_positives: Legitimate network logons (backup agents, admin tools, scheduled tasks with stored credentials).
query:
any where event.code == "4624"
  and winlog.event_data.LogonType == "3"
  and winlog.event_data.TargetLogonId != "0x0"
  and user.name != null
  and not user.name : ("*$", "SYSTEM", "LOCAL SERVICE", "NETWORK SERVICE")

name: C0015 | R14b | Elevated Privileges Assigned to Non-System Account
description: Detects Security 4672 (special privileges assigned to a new logon) for a real account - the elevated-login signal complementary to R14a.
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S7/S8b: elevated logon(s) used for WMI/SMB administration. Building block: ON - combine with R14a for the network-logon + special-privileges story.

## Data and schedule

Security channel, index logs-system.security-c0015*. Interval 1m, look-back 5m.

## Investigation

A 4672 immediately before wmiprvse->rundll32 (R17) on the same host completes the lateral-movement chain.
false_positives: Legitimate admin console/RDP logons also produce 4672.
query:
any where event.code == "4672"
  and winlog.event_data.SubjectLogonId != "0x0"
  and user.name != null
  and not user.name : ("*$", "SYSTEM", "LOCAL SERVICE", "NETWORK SERVICE")

name: C0015 | R15 | LSASS Access with Credential-Access Grant
description: Detects OpenProcess on lsass.exe with a credential-access access mask (0x1010/0x1418/0x1fffff) from a non-system source via Sysmon E10 (S7b, T1003.001).
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S7b credential-access surface. System/ambient sources (wininit/csrss/services/svchost/MsMpEng/Registry/wmiprvse) and query-info-only grants (0x1000/0x101000) are excluded. E10 access alone does not prove credential extraction.

## Data and schedule

Sysmon Operational, index logs-windows.sysmon_operational-c0015*. Interval 1m, look-back 5m.

## Investigation

Identify the source process (name/entity/account); join its E1 for the command line; look for decoy/dump files (E11 lsass*.dmp) as confirmation context.
false_positives: AV/EDR or administration tools (ProcDump, Process Explorer) legitimately touching lsass.
query:
any where event.code == "10"
  and winlog.event_data.TargetImage : "*lsass.exe"
  and winlog.event_data.GrantedAccess : ("0x1010", "0x1418", "0x1fffff")
  and not process.name : ("lsass.exe", "wininit.exe", "csrss.exe", "services.exe", "svchost.exe", "winlogon.exe", "MsMpEng.exe", "Registry", "wmiprvse.exe")
  and not user.name : ("SYSTEM", "LOCAL SERVICE", "NETWORK SERVICE", "*$")

name: C0015 | R16 | Admin Share Access (SMB)
description: Detects access to admin shares (C$/ADMIN$) recorded by Security 5145 - an access check whose strongest instrument is the S8a tool handoff (T1570). Requires the Detailed File Share audit policy; the predicate does not distinguish read, write or result outcomes.
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S8a lateral tool transfer. Sysmon E11 on the SMB target does not keep UNC path/user information, so Security 5145 is the authoritative source. The rule matches share/path only - it is an access indicator, not a write-specific detector.

## Data and schedule

Security channel, index logs-system.security-c0015*. Interval 1m, look-back 5m. ShareName values carry a \\* prefix - the pattern uses "*\\C$".

## Investigation

Verify account, share and relative path; correlate with R14a (network logon) via logon id; match the written file with E11 on the target.
false_positives: Legitimate backup/administration copies over admin shares.
query:
any where event.code == "5145"
  and winlog.event_data.ObjectType : "File"
  and winlog.event_data.ShareName : ("*\\C$", "*\\C$\\*", "*\\ADMIN$", "*\\ADMIN$\\*")
  and winlog.event_data.RelativeTargetName != null

name: C0015 | R17 | WMI-Spawned Process Loading an Unsigned Module
description: Detects the WMI pivot: wmiprvse.exe spawns a process which loads an unsigned module (E1 then E7, joined by entity) - the S8b signature (T1047 + T1218.011).
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S8b WMI remote process creation ending in the DLL surrogate. E7 events carry event.category=library, so the second step uses [any where event.code=="7"].

## Data and schedule

Sysmon Operational, index logs-windows.sysmon_operational-c0015*. Sequence joined by process.entity_id, maxspan 60s.

## Investigation

Verify E1 (parent=wmiprvse, integrity level) -> E7 (Signed=false, hash) -> E11 marker -> new beacon -> E3 egress (R18); correlate with the logon pair (R14a/R14b) in the same window.
false_positives: Software installers using WMI and loading unsigned drivers/modules (rare).
query:
sequence by host.id with maxspan=60s
  [process where event.code == "1"
     and event.type == "start"
     and process.parent.name : "wmiprvse.exe"
     and process.name : ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "rundll32.exe", "regsvr32.exe", "mshta.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
     and process.entity_id != null and not process.entity_id : ("", "{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}", "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")
  ] by process.entity_id
  [any where event.code == "7"
     and winlog.event_data.Signed : "false"
     and process.entity_id != null and not process.entity_id : ("", "{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}", "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")
  ] by process.entity_id

name: C0015 | R18 | Proxy-Spawned PowerShell Making an Egress Connection
description: Detects PowerShell spawned by rundll32/regsvr32 (signed-proxy) making an egress connection (E1 then E3, joined by entity) - the second-session beacon (S9, T1071.001).
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S9 second session established by the DLL surrogate. E3 direction=egress with a non-empty destination.

## Data and schedule

Sysmon Operational, index logs-windows.sysmon_operational-c0015*. Sequence joined by process.entity_id, maxspan 120s (E3 timestamps lag E1 by 2-3s).

## Investigation

Verify rundll32 -> powershell -> egress; compare timestamps with the server-side receipt (ART-07-01); a regular polling interval to a high port is a beacon signature.
false_positives: COM/plugins legitimately starting PowerShell from rundll32 (rare).
query:
sequence by host.id with maxspan=120s
  [process where event.code == "1"
     and event.type == "start"
     and process.name : ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
     and process.parent.name : ("rundll32.exe", "regsvr32.exe")
     and process.entity_id != null and not process.entity_id : ("", "{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}", "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")
  ] by process.entity_id
  [network where event.code == "3"
     and network.direction == "egress"
     and destination.ip != null
     and destination.port != null
     and process.entity_id != null and not process.entity_id : ("", "{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}", "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000")
  ] by process.entity_id

name: C0015 | R19 | RDP Interactive Logon by Non-System Account
description: Detects RDP interactive logon (Security 4624 LogonType 10) by a real account - the day-2 RDP movement of the campaign (S12, T1021.001).
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S12 remote desktop movement. Requires the Logon/Logoff audit policy (success) and the Other Logon/Logoff Events subcategory for 4778/4779 session events. Note: LogonType 3/4 alone (network/batch) do not prove a successful interactive RDP session; only Type 10 (RemoteInteractive) does.

## Data and schedule

Security channel, index logs-system.security-c0015*. Interval 1m, look-back 5m.

## Investigation

Confirm the source IP (winlog.event_data.IpAddress) and correlate the TargetLogonId with R14b; an out-of-hours type-10 logon on a server host is a strong lateral-movement signal.
false_positives: Legitimate IT remote administration over RDP.
query:
any where event.code == "4624"
  and winlog.event_data.LogonType == "10"
  and winlog.event_data.TargetUserName != null
  and not winlog.event_data.TargetUserName : ("*$", "SYSTEM", "LOCAL SERVICE", "NETWORK SERVICE")

name: C0015 | R20 | Portable Remote-Access or Process Tool Dropped and Executed
description: Detects a portable tool (remote-access software: AnyDesk/RustDesk/TeamViewer; process-administration utility: ProcessHacker) dropped into a non-standard location (Videos or drive root) and executed - E11 then E1 sequence (S13, T1219.002 for remote access; ProcessHacker maps to process-discovery tooling, not remote access).
author: C0015 Lab
note:
## Scope

S13 tool deployment mirroring the report (AnyDesk under Videos\, ProcessHacker at C:\ root). The sequence joins by host.name only - it does not prove that the executed binary is the dropped file; treat as correlation.

## Data and schedule

Sysmon Operational, index logs-windows.sysmon_operational-c0015*. Sequence of 2 events (drop then run), maxspan 10m, joined by host.name.

## Investigation

Confirm the binary hash against vendor signatures; check the tool's connection targets (E3) - public relays versus lab-local listeners; correlate with R15 if the tool touches lsass.
false_positives: Users manually installing legitimate remote-control software.
query:
sequence by host.name with maxspan=10m
  [any where event.code == "11" and file.path : ("*\\Videos\\*", "C:\\*.exe") and file.extension == "exe"]
  [any where event.code == "1" and process.name : ("AnyDesk*", "RustDesk*", "TeamViewer*", "ProcessHacker*")]
